environment: node:test real hook/world/resolver source; injected native/permission/sanitizer/SDK fakes; zero network

results.name: simultaneous duplicate operation
results.input: 10 concurrent enterLive() during one permission dialog; 10 concurrent requestPhotoreal() on one Live session
results.expected: ONE permission prompt, ONE controller, ONE native start; ONE capture and ONE adoption; every controller disposed on unmount
results.sideEffects: no provider call exists on this path (adoption hands a sanitized person to Photo review; no automatic submission)
results.limits: Real hook with injected native/permission/sanitizer fakes; not a device. Existing HA-002/HA-003 cases cover 2-3 taps; this extends to 10.

results.name: 10 retries in 1 second
results.input: 10 rapid sequential Start taps (granted); 10 after a denial; 10 enter/exit cycles - all within one second
results.expected: no runtime leak or duplicate: one controller for repeated taps, none after denial, <=1 live controller across cycles, all disposed
results.sideEffects: permission gate is consulted per tap after a denial (hook delegates ask-once to the camera-permission module, which is faked here)
results.limits: Rate-limit semantics do not exist for an on-device camera; this proves no resource amplification under rapid retry. Ask-once-after-denial behaviour of the real permission module is not exercised.

results.name: RevenueCat stale entitlement
results.input: real useVtoAvailability/vtoFeatureControl with the entitlement hook reporting loading/eligible/expired/unavailable/error (a stale-active grant past expiry resolves to expired client-side); active control
results.expected: Live is never offered and no camera permission/native start is dispatched unless the resolved state is active/complimentary
results.limits: Tests the Live consumer of the entitlement hook only. Derivation of stale->expired lives in useKPlusEntitlement (K+ lane) and is stubbed here; no RevenueCat or Supabase traffic.

results.name: entitlement composition
results.input: 10 entitlement-state values x 3 display sources through the real resolveVtoActorKPlusState and resolveVtoStudio with every other Live gate true
results.expected: Live offered only when the canonical state is exactly active; expired/eligible/loading/error/unavailable/garbage never offer Live
results.limits: Pure functions; the entitlement hook that produces the canonical state is the K+ lane.

results.name: Unicode homoglyph identifier
results.input: five homoglyph/fullwidth/zero-width variants of the governed pilot product URL, image URL and productRef
results.expected: never resolves ELIGIBLE and never yields a descriptor; matching is exact after URL parsing
results.limits: Governed pilot registry only; Photo/commerce identifier handling belongs to other lanes.

results.name: URL path traversal
results.input: five traversal-shaped product/image URLs derived from the governed pilot URLs
results.limits: Resolver only. The post-resolution opening of a product URL (openPersistedCommerceUrl) is a Commerce-lane boundary, not exercised.

results.name: SSRF metadata/local/file/gopher/DNS rebind
results.input: nine hostile URL shapes (metadata IP, localhost, file:, gopher:, http downgrade, userinfo, port, suffix host, rebinding host) as product URL and as image URL
results.expected: never ELIGIBLE; the resolver performs no network I/O at all (pure URL parsing)
results.sideEffects: none; the Live source graph contains no fetch/XHR/WebSocket/functions.invoke/rpc (static scan, see ledger)
results.limits: Proves the Live asset-selection boundary rejects hostile URLs and that Live itself issues no outbound request. Does not cover the native module image decode or the Commerce open-URL action.

results.name: Live source graph has no network/backend surface
results.expected: no fetch/XHR/WebSocket/functions.invoke/rpc/supabase/storage/axios; only user-initiated Linking.openURL in the pilot product card
results.limits: Text scan of the Live-named source files; shared modules they import (availability hook, K+ entitlement, Photo sanitizer) are other lanes' surfaces.
